$comment: Rule catalog — edge. Standard 14. Carries one prohibition: fabricating edge. Edge is a difference between two probabilities, which is what makes it recomputable and therefore the one quantity here a checker can settle exactly.

rules.title: Edge is stated only against a market reference
rules.description: A record stating an edge also carries a market-implied probability to measure it against.
rules.rationale: Edge means the difference between this prediction and the reference expectation. With no reference there is no difference, and a stated edge is measuring against something the record never names.
rules.remediation: Supply the market reference, or remove the edge.

rules.title: The stated edge equals the difference it claims to be
rules.description: The stated edge equals the predicted probability minus the market-implied probability, within the project's tolerance.
rules.rationale: The edge is the number decisions are made on, and it is the easiest place for a sign error or a stale market quote to hide. Since it is fully determined by two other numbers in the record, disagreement is always a real defect.
rules.remediation: Recompute the edge from the current values of both probabilities.

rules.title: Edge is not fabricated
rules.description: A stated edge is derived from a declared market reference and reproduces on recomputation; it is never asserted independently of the numbers it claims to relate.
rules.rationale: An edge is the number that justifies acting. Fabricating one — asserting a figure that does not follow from the prediction and the market — invents the entire case for the decision, and unlike a fabricated probability it is fully checkable, so there is no reason to accept it on trust.
rules.remediation: Derive the edge from the record's own probability and market-implied probability, or remove it.
